findings.description: ADR 0114 corrects decision 113's claim that blobIsBinary's `<rev>:<path>` is safe, but lacks the `- Amends: [0113](0113-pup-s-git-pins-core-bigfilethreshold-a-diff.md)` line that docs/adr/README.md requires for the cross-references a decision states (0113 itself carries `- Amends: [0053]`).

The added paragraph in `diffHunks`' JSDoc restates the WHY that the `PATH_AS_GIVEN` JSDoc already gives (macOS NFD-to-NFC rewrite, decision 114); AGENTS.md §Comments says to delete the call-site copy when the seam already says it, as the neighbouring DIFF_SAFE_FLAGS pins do.

The decision-114 tests can only fail on macOS (git builds its precompose code only for Darwin), and the only workflow here (.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml) runs on ubuntu-latest, so if a later change drops PATH_AS_GIVEN no automated run will catch it. The ADR acknowledges this ('On macOS, each test fails with its pin removed'). A darwin CI job, or a comment pointing to macOS-only verification, would make the guard real.

This is the third copy of the same macOS rewrite explanation, after the `PATH_AS_GIVEN` JSDoc and the ADR. Only the last sentence, "Elsewhere git ignores the key and these pass either way", is new. It is a useful WHY, because it explains why the tests don't fail on Linux. Trim the comment to that sentence plus "(decision 114)".

`PATH_AS_GIVEN` sits about 85 lines below `DIFF_SAFE_FLAGS` (line 417), the existing per-call pin constant. Unlike `DIFF_SAFE_FLAGS`, it has no `as const`. Placing the two together would keep the per-call pins in one place.

`PATH_AS_GIVEN` is spliced by hand into three git argv arrays (diffHunks and both cat-file calls in blobIsBinary), so any future git call taking a path or `<rev>:<path>` must remember to add it; the ADR deliberately keeps it out of GIT_SAFE_CONFIG, so this is only a note.

The line "as two files, because the index takes any bytes; only a working tree on APFS cannot. Given `é.ts` spelled NFD, the per-file" runs well past the ~90-column wrap of the surrounding lines. It looks like a reflow leftover.
